{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZgaFqA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDHiBg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 43, "title": "Separate inline session visibility from immersive frame suspension", "body": "## Problem

At `dev` commit `325a10bb133f397b097ad0bf784d8c8f889a02ab`, immersive startup makes existing and newly created inline sessions report `hidden`, even when their document remains visible. Document visibility transitions are then masked, and immersive shutdown fabricates a return-to-visible event. Applications observing session visibility receive incorrect state and notifications.

The defect is in [runtime.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/325a10bb133f397b097ad0bf784d8c8f889a02ab/src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts#L163). [Conformance assertions](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/325a10bb133f397b097ad0bf784d8c8f889a02ab/tests/conformance.ts#L280) and inventory revision 12 encode the same mistake.

## Expected outcome

Inline visibility follows its document, while inline animation loops remain suspended during immersive presentation. Applications receive truthful visibility events and retain correctly queued callbacks across suspension and resumption.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. This is core `inline` behavior; no additional feature descriptor is needed. Preserve viewer-only inline negotiation, Quest 3 selected `immersive-vr`/`immersive-ar` modes, Android `immersive-ar`, and existing immersive-concurrency `InvalidStateError` behavior.

**Retained AI requirement correction:** The original runtime/fixture/inventory assumption was that immersive presentation makes inline sessions hidden. **Correction:** [Device CRD, 9 June 2026, §4.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#xrsession-interface) requires document-mirrored inline visibility; [§4.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#animation-frames) separately specifies inline loop suspension during immersive sessions. **Rationale:** scheduling suppression must not manufacture visibility changes. Section 12.6 requires `XRSessionEvent` notifications when visibility changes.

`XRSystem` already tracks immersive ownership, and `_finish()` handles explicit/device-driven shutdown. Keep scheduling suppression separate from the document listener. Relevant dependencies are Playwright 1.64.0, tsx 4.23.15 and TypeScript 5.9.3; no dependency upgrade is indicated.

Reuse the genuine extension/panel routes in `tests/reference-space-browser.ts`, `tests/cdp-target.ts` and `tests/firefox-driver.ts`. The [pinned WPT visibility case](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/e1859580b5fcf74940a18d2f783296b4961035e3/webxr/xrSession_visibilityState_inline.https.html) supplies hide/restore assertions requiring adaptation. The existing `test:wpt` selection does not include it. #41/#42 reported passing shutdown checks, not this correction. Historical broad partial outcomes are not completion evidence; deferred modules remain in scope.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Existing and newly created live inline sessions mirror actual `document.visibilityState` before, during and after immersive presentation. Immersive entry/exit alone produces no inline visibility event. State remains stable during XR animation-frame processing.
- [ ] Actual document hide/show produces one corresponding `XRSessionEvent` per transition through listeners and `onvisibilitychange`, with the owning `event.session`. Repeated unchanged notifications produce no duplicate events, including while inline rendering is suspended.
- [ ] Preserve suspension independently: inline callbacks remain queued during immersive presentation; cancellation remains effective. With valid inline base layers, surviving callbacks resume once eligible, in registration order, and render to their own canvases. Cover multiple inline sessions created before/during presentation, immersive end while hidden, restoration afterward, and explicit/device-driven exit. Ended inline sessions deliver no later callbacks or document-driven events and release their listeners.
- [ ] Replace contradictory conformance assertions and documentation together with runtime/generated-bundle changes. Preserve immersive rendering, negotiation and #41 shutdown behavior. Retain historical reports with an explicit correction reference.
- [ ] Add focused executable cases using the existing Chromium and Firefox helpers, covering Quest VR, Quest MR and Android AR configurations plus inline-only operation. Adapt the pinned WPT assertions and exercise native document hide/restore; overriding only `document.hidden` is insufficient. Disclose any additional deterministic scheduling instrumentation.
- [ ] Coordinator runs `npm run build:firefox`, the documented focused visibility commands for both browsers, and `git diff --check` before merge. Record exact commands, browser/tool versions, tested source/bundle hashes, observed states/events/callbacks/pixels, failures, skips and cleanup. Distinguish fixture existence from execution; add no generic application rerun or independent AI re-review.
- [ ] Retain the original assumption, correction, primary source and rationale in this Issue/resulting PR. Further mistaken AI requirements may be corrected with the same evidence record without human approval or independent AI re-review. Preserve the goal and meaningful acceptance; do not weaken requirements to accommodate unfinished code or failures.

## Optional validation

None required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. The Coordinator owns implementation, tests and normal PR review.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
